newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alpargatas closes convertible deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alpargatas closes convertible deal.

text.p: Argentina's Alpargatas SAIC on Thursday said it successfully placed 80 million pesos of mandatory convertible subordinated bonds due 2003.
The placement was made together with warrants to subscribe 75 common shares at one peso each, said the textile and footwear manufacturer said in a statement.
Alpargatas shares rose to three centavos to 89 on Thursday.
The offering was underwritten by Newbridge Latin America LP, a private U.S. equity fund, which bought about 44 million pesos of the convertible bonds.

Under an earlier agreement between Newbridge and Alpargatas, Newbridge will become a major shareholder in the Argentine company through its purchase. The deal allows Newbridge to designate three of eleven Alpargatas directors.

Alpargatas said the issuance of the convertibles, to be listed on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange by year-end, is part of a plan to reduce short-term liabilities and lengthen the duration of its debt portfolio.
As a part of this plan, Alpargatas hopes to issue a medium-term bond of up to $150 million in the fourth quarter.
